Trend Summary Statistics

Source: R/stats.R
trend_summary.Rd

Computes trend statistics and monitoring-period summary metrics for environmental time-series data.

trend_summary(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
trend_summary(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  method = "mann_kendall",
  censored_method = "cenken",
  conf.level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
trend_summary(
  df,
  method = "mann_kendall",
  censored_method = "cenken",
  conf.level = 0.95
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location_id

Location column name.

param_name

Analyte column name.

sample_date

Sample date column name.

analysis_result

Analytical result column name.

method

Trend method. One of:

  • `"lm"` Linear regression

  • `"loess"` Local regression smoother

  • `"gam"` Generalized additive model

  • `"mann_kendall"` Mann-Kendall trend test

censored_method

Method used to handle censored data. One of:

  • `"cenken"` Censored Kendall trend estimator

  • `"as_reported"` Use analytical results as reported

conf.level

Confidence level used for trend estimates.

Value

A tibble containing one row per trend group.

The returned table includes:

n

Number of records in the group.

first_date

Earliest sample date.

last_date

Latest sample date.

date_range_days

Monitoring period length in days.

date_range_years

Monitoring period length in years.

sampling_frequency

Approximate samples collected per year.

minimum_concentration

Minimum analytical result.

median_concentration

Median analytical result.

mean_concentration

Mean analytical result.

maximum_concentration

Maximum analytical result.

standard_deviation

Sample standard deviation.

coefficient_of_variation

Standard deviation divided by mean.

trend_method

Trend estimation method used.

censored_method

Censored-data handling method used.

slope

Estimated trend slope.

p_value

Trend test p-value.

conf_low

Lower confidence limit for the slope estimate.

conf_high

Upper confidence limit for the slope estimate.

significant

TRUE when the trend is statistically significant at the specified confidence level.

trend_direction

Increasing, Decreasing, or Stable.

Details

For `env_schema` objects, trend calculations are performed using the standardized `.analysis_result` values and schema mappings. This ensures trends are evaluated consistently regardless of the original source column names.

If the input is grouped with [dplyr::group_by()], trend summaries are calculated within the existing groups. For ungrouped inputs, summaries are calculated separately for each location and analyte.

Trend calculations require at least three non-missing observations and at least two distinct analytical result values. Groups that do not meet these requirements return summary metrics, but trend-specific fields such as `slope`, `p_value`, `conf_low`, and `conf_high` are returned as `NA`.

Slope estimates and significance statistics are only available for trend methods that support formal trend estimation. For smoothing methods such as `"loess"` and `"gam"`, these fields are returned as `NA`.

For Mann-Kendall analyses using `censored_method = "cenken"`, confidence limits for the Sen slope are not currently available and are returned as `NA`.

For ungrouped `env_schema` inputs, trends are calculated by:

  • the mapped location variable returned by `location_var()`

  • the mapped analyte variable returned by `analyte_var()`

Confidence intervals are available for some trend methods. When a confidence interval cannot be estimated, `conf_low` and `conf_high` are returned as `NA`.

env_schema Method

For `env_schema` objects, `trend_summary()` automatically uses the schema mappings and standardized analytical fields:

  • `.analysis_result`

  • `.censored`

  • mapped location variable

  • mapped analyte variable

This allows trend summaries to remain consistent regardless of the original source column names or schema mappings used by the input data.

Examples

trend_summary(gw)
#> # A tibble: 387 × 22
#>    location_id param_name              n first_date          last_date          
#>    <chr>       <chr>               <int> <dttm>              <dttm>             
#>  1 MW-1        Alkalinity, total …    20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  2 MW-1        Aluminum, dissolved    19 2008-02-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  3 MW-1        Antimony, dissolved    20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  4 MW-1        Arsenic, dissolved     21 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  5 MW-1        Barium, dissolved      20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  6 MW-1        Beryllium, dissolv…    20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  7 MW-1        Boron, dissolved       20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  8 MW-1        Cadmium, dissolved     20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#>  9 MW-1        Calcium, dissolved     20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#> 10 MW-1        Chloride, total        20 2007-12-20 00:00:00 2013-10-02 00:00:00
#> # ℹ 377 more rows
#> # ℹ 17 more variables: date_range_days <dbl>, date_range_years <dbl>,
#> #   sampling_frequency <dbl>, minimum_concentration <dbl>,
#> #   median_concentration <dbl>, mean_concentration <dbl>,
#> #   maximum_concentration <dbl>, standard_deviation <dbl>,
#> #   coefficient_of_variation <dbl>, trend_method <chr>, censored_method <chr>,
#> #   slope <dbl>, p_value <dbl>, conf_low <dbl>, conf_high <dbl>, …

gw |>
  dplyr::group_by(location_id) |>
  trend_summary()
